content.title: THE AISLE SNACK FOR THAT {{AWKWARD}} BLOATED FEELING
facts: **Fennel seeds** – chew 1/2 tsp after a heavy meal, they relax gut muscles and push trapped gas through faster.
**Papaya** – 1 cup fresh (not canned) has papain, an enzyme that breaks down protein so your stomach isn't stuck doing all the work.
**Ginger tea** – 1 cup steeped fresh ginger speeds up stomach emptying, so that heavy, stuck feeling after eating fades quicker.
**Cucumber** – 90% water plus quercetin, a combo that eases swelling in the gut lining after a salty meal.
**Peppermint tea** – 1 cup between meals relaxes the intestinal wall, taking the edge off cramping and pressure.
**Pineapple** – 1/2 cup has bromelain, another protein-digesting enzyme that works especially well after meat-heavy meals.
**Plain yogurt** – 1 small bowl with live cultures helps rebalance gut bacteria that get thrown off by processed food.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
Fennel seeds are an old trick worth bringing back — chewing just half a teaspoon slowly signals your digestive muscles to relax, which is why trapped gas moves on instead of sitting there uncomfortably. Papaya works differently: it's packed with papain, an enzyme your own stomach doesn't always produce enough of, so it basically does pre-digestion work for you on heavier meals. Ginger is the one to reach for when you feel stuffed and sluggish — it speeds up how fast your stomach empties its contents into the intestine, which shortens that uncomfortable "heavy" window. Everyone's gut reacts a little differently though, so pay attention to what actually settles yours.
